keyChanges.title: Q2 earnings: Musk confirms Optimus has no supply chain and a 'flat and long' ramp — still no production units or commercial path
keyChanges.description: On Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call and in the Q2 shareholder update, management finally answered the production-ramp questions investors had queued — and the answers lowered expectations. Official letter language: Fremont Model S/X lines are decommissioned; Tesla is 'installing the first-generation lines for Optimus, where we expect to start production soon' / 'anticipated production later this year.' Initial builds 'will be used in our Optimus Academy for training data collection and further functionality development.' Giga Texas Optimus site development is 'in full swing' but still construction, not output. Musk on the call: Optimus is 'the hardest product to scale manufacturing that we've ever made at Tesla because everything on the robot is new'; 'with Optimus, there is no supply chain' so Tesla must build it from scratch or insource; the manufacturing S-curve's 'initial portion… will be quite flat and long'; reliability fear framed as a 70 kg robot that can 'flop over' if it goes haywire. He still called Optimus Tesla's 'biggest product ever' and floated aspirational Optimus 4 at Austin targeting '10 million units a year versus 1 million units a year of Optimus 3' — with heavy caveats. Capex is >$25B for the year; Q2 free cash flow was −$1.09B on $5.8B capex as AI/robotics spend accelerated. Stock fell ~12–14.5% the next day (~$140B market cap), with coverage citing limited new Optimus milestones. Reality: late-July/August full-scale start window is not confirmed as met; letter still says 'soon'/'later this year'; zero disclosed unit counts, yield, takt time, factory deployment tasks, 2027 external sales volume, or pricing; all near-term robots remain internal Academy training units. Competitors (Agility Digit) already generate warehouse revenue while Tesla remains pre-revenue on Optimus.

positive_signals: Official confirmation Fremont first-gen Optimus production lines are being installed after S/X decommission
Giga Texas dedicated Optimus building construction 'in full swing' — multi-site manufacturing path intact
Supply-chain VP Karen Cattan: Tesla will insource parts when partners fall short; Micron memory allocation, TSMC/Samsung fab investments named as enablers
Elluswamy: Optimus can learn factory tasks by observing Tesla workers — data flywheel thesis restated
Musk still frames Optimus as 'biggest product ever' and aspirational Gen 3 1M/yr / Gen 4 10M/yr manufacturing scale
negative_signals: No verified full-scale production start, unit count, yield, or takt time disclosed despite late-July/August target window opening
Shareholder letter only: 'expect to start production soon' / 'anticipated production later this year' — softer than a firm start confirmation
Musk: no existing Optimus supply chain; hardest manufacturing scale-up in Tesla history; initial S-curve 'quite flat and long'
First builds explicitly for Optimus Academy internal training/data only — not factory labor replacement or external sales
No 2027 external sales volume, pricing, commercial customers, or factory deployment task list answered despite top investor question
Reliability framed as unsolved (70 kg robot that can flop over) — not ready for unsupervised field work
Aspirational Optimus 4 10M/yr is far-future messaging, not near-term capacity
Capex >$25B and −$1.09B FCF; market erased ~$140B as AI/robotics 'just trust me' narrative failed to deliver milestones
Electrek/critical coverage: generalized-task claim is industry-wide pitch, not Tesla-proven advantage; mass production still 'somewhere down the road'
Competitors already commercializing small-scale warehouse robots while Optimus remains pre-revenue

key_metrics.actual: First-gen Fremont lines installing; production 'soon'/later 2026; initial units → Optimus Academy only; 0 commercial units; 0 disclosed production rate
key_metrics.target: Prior: full-scale Fremont late July–August 2026; investor ask: factory deployment + 2027 external sales volume; pay package still implies 1M Optimus units
key_metrics.trajectory: Facility conversion progressing but management officially telegraphing flat, long, supply-chain-constrained ramp; commercialization still 2027+ with no roadmap numbers

keyChanges.title: Tesla app quietly builds Optimus phone-key and in-home data consent — software shell years ahead of product
keyChanges.description: Code analysis of Tesla iOS app v4.59.0 (reported July 22, 2026 by Teslarati and TeslaNorth via @Tesla_App_iOS) shows groundwork for Optimus in the consumer app: a dedicated Bluetooth Low Energy 'Robot' phone-key authentication stack (also likely shared with Cybercab), a home data-collection consent screen for video/spatial data while Optimus performs in-home tasks, and robot system alerts (low battery, mechanical issues). This is product-software plumbing, not a production or capability milestone. Combined with earnings confirmation that 2026 units go to Optimus Academy for training only, the app work is a multi-year consumer-path placeholder — useful signal that Tesla is designing a home-robot control surface, but it does not move unit output, factory deployment, or 2027 external sales readiness.

positive_signals: App-level Robot phone key + home consent UI implies long-term productization planning beyond factory demos
In-home video/spatial data consent aligns with vision-learning thesis for household tasks
Corroborated by both Teslarati and TeslaNorth from same app reverse-engineering source
negative_signals: Strings/code only — no live Optimus consumer feature, no pre-orders, no pricing
Earnings same day confirmed 2026 builds are internal Academy training units, not home robots
Does not address manufacturing ramp, supply chain, yield, or commercial timeline gaps
Consumer Optimus still targeted end-2027 at earliest; app prep can sit idle for 18+ months
